name: Nothing reaches the screen until something has vouched for it
insight: Elapsed time is never admissible as evidence about pixels, but is admissible as evidence about a correspondent's silence; a deadline's only reachable outcome is a held cover plus retry, never a reveal
field_standard: timeout-backed reveal on top of the frame-presented callback; generation counters for stale async results
evidence: 120 enumerated combinations assert the invariant after every step (transitionCoordinator.test.ts:298-357), verified by running the suite
weaknesses: named executable invariant is test-only, not a production guard
test product is 120 cases not the 6-axis product claimed; ordering not permuted
confidence label never leaves an in-page debug array
frame callback lacking timecode metadata is still labelled strong evidence and skips admissibility checks
coordinator poster-cover branch is dead in production

name: Content that has to earn the right to be shown live
insight: One publish-time execution mints both the runtime permission to show live pixels and the exact substitute image used when that permission is denied, keyed on one identity so they cannot drift
field_standard: upload-time validation, ingest thumbnailing, app-marketplace review, capability probing, CI browser gates — all standard individually
evidence: canary run captures posters (sim-canary-publish.ts:99-171, missing poster is an error); verdict re-derived not read (canaryJudge.ts); one computeConfigHash serves reveal gate, poster key and export PRNG seed (simIdentity.ts:136)
weaknesses: nothing tests that the captured substitute matches the live frame
publish guard accepts single-engine evidence while config defaults to one engine
every revision records both protocol versions as 0
posters never invalidated on the production publication path

name: Deterministic capture of interactive content to linear video
reason: Field standard, matched almost part for part: virtual clock over the same globals, seeded PRNG, pinned headless-shell binary, compositor stepped via the headless frame-control interface. Separately, the reproducibility guarantee is not established — handshake frame offset and compositor clock offset are both host-dependent, the suite asserts a six-frame slack band rather than equality, and the only byte-identity assertion is disabled by default, synthetic, and covers the non-production backend.

name: No-network, credential-free container for untrusted customer code
reason: Textbook container hardening. Argv is genuinely strict and credential-sweep on the job spec is careful, but both container components are marked never-verified-in-container and the file itself states it proves only that the arguments are right.

name: One injected frame-gate serving both live pause and deterministic export
reason: True in code and yields a real no-divergence property, but it is a consequence of document-start injection ordering — the standard technique every tool in this space relies on. The test pinning it uses a five-line stand-in gate; the real-gate test is skipped by default.

name: Naming the package boundary instead of inferring it from the entry file's directory
reason: Incident fix. Correct and obvious in hindsight; the labour was the incident, not the idea.

name: Immutable revisions with atomic compare-and-set pointer flip
reason: Immutable publishing / blue-green applied to content. Textbook.

name: Content-addressed substitute-image cache key covering all appearance axes
reason: Standard content addressing; thoroughness of the key is not invention.

name: Partitioning configuration into rebuild-forcing versus live-applicable fields
reason: Same idea infrastructure-as-code tools have long used to mark which attributes force resource replacement versus in-place update. Standard pattern, different domain.

name: Private transferred message channel to a sandboxed iframe
reason: Documented, widely-blogged standard pattern, recommended for exactly the stale-sender reason cited here.

name: Per-activation identities defeating stale acknowledgements
reason: Generation/epoch tagging is textbook. The six-axis decomposition is careful and the navigation-survives-contentWindow gotcha is good, but neither is inventive.

name: Three-state capability flags (true / false / unknown)
reason: Tri-state optionality where absence is its own case. Standard.

name: Pure reducers making illegal lifecycle states enumerable
reason: State machines are a standard pattern; methodology is not mechanism. It is the reason survivor 1 is provable, and is credited there.

name: Managed section lifecycle contract replacing a single cleanup callback
reason: Standard component lifecycle design. The observation that one teardown hook cannot express suspend/quiesce/release/prove-first-frame is correct and ordinary.

name: Predictive residency of expensive interactive content under a budget
reason: Preloading plus a warm pool. The field does exactly this, including predicting future need from usage traces.

name: Adaptive quality with asymmetric hysteresis
reason: Textbook control design; adaptive-quality managers in the 3D-on-web space are documented as using hysteresis for the same anti-oscillation reason.

name: Closed-loop budget refinement from field telemetry with hostile-input guards
reason: Standard telemetry hygiene for an unauthenticated ingest endpoint: minimum samples, implausible-magnitude rejection, truncated-feed rejection, bounded step.

name: Lab measurement as cold-start prior, refined by field data
reason: The standard approach to cold-start estimation. Requiring the two estimators to span the same steps is a good catch and obvious once stated.

name: Not judging a device against a standard derived from its own population
reason: A real and nicely-written bug fix. 'Do not compare a signal against a reference derived from that same signal' is basic control-loop hygiene.

name: Page-wide lease so one simulation surface does real work at a time
reason: A priority mutex with a broker. Standard.

name: Section-boundary detection from presented frames instead of the coarse progress event
reason: Documented use of the frame callback; the module honestly notes it only moves detection earlier and fixes nothing downstream.

name: Verifying revision immutability against the database rather than path shape
reason: Good catch — customer packages can mimic the system's path grammar and the cost is a one-year immutable cache header on mutable bytes. But 'do not infer trust from a user-controllable path' is a well-known defect class.

name: Per-package browser capability floor by feature detection
reason: Explicitly the documented best practice (detect the feature, never sniff the user-agent), plus the sensible refinement of penalising only packages that need it.

name: Manifest hashing final stored bytes after every rewrite and injection
reason: A build-integrity manifest. The point that a pre-transform hash proves nothing while looking like proof is well put and well known.

name: Crash-safe write ordering for substitute images
reason: Bytes before rows on write, rows before bytes on delete, so a crash leaves the invisible failure. Standard two-store ordering discipline.

name: Deterministic release gate and expand/contract migration audit
reason: Ordinary continuous-delivery discipline plus a schema-migration linter; several mature open-source linters classify migration statements the same way. The audit-and-refuse structure is the standard quality-gate shape.

name: Suspend tracked as explicit debt rather than read from the state machine
reason: Bug fix — the machine deliberately cannot answer the question, so a separate record is the correct repair, not an invention.

name: Eviction victim identified by object instance rather than by key
reason: Bug fix for an ABA hazard. Correct and standard.

name: In-place section-identifier rewrite on project duplication
reason: Bug fix. Surgical byte-preserving rewrite is careful engineering, not invention.

name: Centralised eviction guard replacing five scattered call sites
reason: Obvious refactor after a bug in which three of five sites had the guard and the two that ran did not.
